articles.title: Cost-optimal transmission reduction in early pandemic response: a multi-objective health-economic modelling study across 110 countries
articles.summary: BackgroundEarly pandemic responses must balance transmission control against socioeconomic costs but the strategy that minimises total costs and whether it varies by country remain unknown. We analysed country-specific cost-optimal intervention strategies and examined whether national indices could inform response targets. MethodsWe fitted mechanistic models to the first year of reported COVID-19 cases in 110 countries and assessed structural identifiability and parameter uncertainty. Multi-objective optimisation identified efficient trade-offs between transmission reduction and infections across 26-, 40-, and 52-week horizons without vaccination. We selected cost-minimising strategies using GDP-scaled intervention costs and infection costs incorporating quarantine and mortality. Excess-cost ratios, defined as the relative cost increase over the optimum, quantified deviations from the cost-minimising strategy. We also examined associations with national socioeconomic and health-system indices. ResultsCost-optimal average transmission reduction ranged from 31.2% to 57.3% across countries. Across the time horizons, the mean excess-cost ratio for 110 countries was 55.2% (median 30.8%). Excess costs increased asymmetrically around the country-specific optimal transmission reduction: a five-percentage-point transmission reduction below the optimum was associated with excess-cost ratios exceeding 400%, compared with 10-80% for an equivalent increase above the optimum. The range of transmission reduction associated with excess-cost ratios below 40% widened 1.47-fold as the horizon increased from 26 to 52 weeks. Among national indices, the Socio-Demographic Index (SDI) and GDP per capita had the largest redundancy indices (0.40 and 0.37, respectively). ConclusionsUnder the modelled assumptions, transmission reduction below the country-specific optimum resulted in greater excess costs than reduction above the optimum, highlighting the potential value of precautionary early-response strategies when intervention effectiveness is uncertain. National socioeconomic and health-system indices may provide a broad indication of cost-optimal intervention intensity, although country-specific conditions remain important. These findings provide a quantitative framework for balancing intervention intensity, infection burden, and economic costs across diverse national settings. What is already known on this topic During the COVID-19 pandemic, both infections and control measures caused substantial economic losses, creating a trade-off between reducing infection-related costs and limiting intervention costs. Pandemic preparedness and health-system infrastructure have been assessed using national indices such as the GHS and UHC indices. What this study adds Across 110 countries, this study compares model-inferred responses with modelled costoptimal strategies, quantifying excess costs under explicit epidemiological and economic assumptions. In four illustrative countries, modelled costs increased more after a five-percentage-point shortfall below the optimum than after an equivalent increase above it. National indices showed descriptive associations with modelled outcomes but did not establish validated country-specific transmission reduction targets. How this study might affect research, practice or policy Policymakers could evaluate precautionary early-response margins when intervention effectiveness is uncertain, while recognising that the appropriate margin depends on local conditions and cost assumptions. Preparedness plans could combine national indices with locally calibrated models and explicit assessment of feasibility, affordability and the distribution of costs.

articles.title: Influence of COVID-19 and COVID-19 rumours on trust and uptake of single-dose male HPV vaccination in the Add-Vacc cluster-randomised trial, northwest Tanzania.
articles.summary: PMID: 42854550. DOI: 10.1016/j.vaccine.2026.129231. BackgroundThe COVID-19 pandemic impacted public health services and vaccination uptake globally. Trust in health services and vaccination programmes is critical for vaccine acceptance. Between 2020 and 2022, Tanzania shifted its acknowledgement of COVID-19 and its prevention strategies. National COVID-19 vaccination coverage reached 51% by April 2023. The Add-Vacc cluster-randomised trial (CRT) provided single-dose, human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination to 14-18-year-old males in 2023-2024, the first time HPV vaccination was offered to young men in Tanzania. The Tanzania national vaccination programme promotes HPV vaccination for girls as the vaccine to prevent cervical cancer.ObjectiveThis qualitative study investigated the influence of vaccine and COVID-19 rumours on uptake of male HPV vaccination offered through the trial.MethodsBetween May 2023 to May 2024, field teams collected rumours data using an electronic-rumours tracking tool, key informant interviews, in-depth interviews, focus group discussions and rapid ethnography with stakeholders including adolescents, parents, teachers, health workers and community leaders.ResultsData from community members, including youth, indicated that changes in Tanzania's COVID-19 policies between 2020 and 2022 prompted mistrust and concerns about the trial vaccine. Documented concerns included questions regarding the motives of national leadership and vaccination programmes, rumours that the vaccine offered through the trial was a concealed COVID-19 vaccine or was for- depopulation or led to changes in fertility and/or male virility. Rapid assessment of trial-related rumours and responsive, ongoing community engagement activities to address rumours supported efforts to enhance vaccination uptake and acceptance.ConclusionShifting COVID-19 policies during the height of the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic subsequently influenced trust and HPV vaccine acceptance during the vaccination phase of the Add-Vacc CRT. Documenting and monitoring community concerns early in a project delivering a vaccine to a new population group can inform ongoing, dynamic community engagement aimed towards promoting dialogue and building trust across stakeholder groups and implementation teams.

articles.title: Ethnic disparities in COVID-19 vaccine uptake among among 55+ year-old Canadians: Exploring the role of racial discrimination, chronic disease comorbidities, and conspiracy beliefs.
articles.summary: PMID: 42837895. DOI: 10.1016/j.vaccine.2026.129213. BackgroundCanada's COVID-19 vaccination program achieved high overall coverage, yet older racialized and Indigenous people experienced lower uptake and far higher infection and mortality rates. Structural inequities, low health literacy, mistrust, and misinformation contributed to these gaps. Despite early vaccine prioritization, little disaggregated data exist for racialized and Indigenous older adults. This study examines vaccine uptake in these underserved groups to inform more equitable public health strategies and strengthen future pandemic responses.MethodsWe conducted a Canada-wide cross-sectional online survey of adults aged ≥55 years in March 2025 using Computer-Assisted Web Interviewing. Participants completed measures assessing COVID-19 vaccination doses, experiences of major racial discrimination, conspiracy beliefs, health literacy, chronic conditions, and sociodemographic characteristics.ResultsOf the 581participants, 90,3% received at least one dose. Black and Indigenous people were more often unvaccinated (17%), compared to 5.5-6% for Asians and Arabs. Receipt of ≥5 doses was observed in 50% of White, 41.8% of Asian and 13.8% of Black individuals. Older adults (≥65 years) had greater uptake (OR=1.58, 95%CI: 1.07-2.32), as did retirees (OR=2.47) and more highly educated participants (college OR=2.29; Bachelor OR=2.77). Higher conspiracy belief scores were significantly associated with lower odds of receiving higher doses (OR=0.91, 95%CI: 0.89-0.93; p<0.001). Additionally, a greater number of chronic diseases was associated with higher odds of being in a higher vaccine-dose category (OR = 1.09, 95% CI: 1.02-1.18).ConclusionDespite pandemic efforts, substantial ethnic disparities in COVID-19 vaccine uptake persisted, with lower coverage in racialized and Indigenous groups. Addressing structural inequities, comorbidities, and misinformation is critical to achieving more equitable, culturally responsive vaccination strategies.

articles.title: Perception of COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness perception in older racialized communities: role of major racial discrimination and health literacy.
articles.summary: PMID: 42832932. DOI: 10.1016/j.vaccine.2026.129214. ObjectiveVaccination has been scientifically proven to be safe and to prevent infectious diseases. The COVID-19 vaccine has been crucial in combating the pandemic. In Canada, despite widespread vaccine hesitancy, little has specifically addressed older adults from racialized communities. This study investigates perceptions of COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness among older adults by racial background, examining the influence of major racial discrimination and health literacy.Study designA cross-sectional pan-Canadian study.MethodsData were collected using Computer-Assisted Web Interviewing (March 2025). The COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness was tested with t-tests, ANOVA, and multivariable linear regression.Results581 participants were included: Arab (11.5%), Asian (15.8%), Black (16.2%), Indigenous (9%), and White (35.8%); including men (48.2%), women (43.0%), and 8.8% identifying as non-binary. Participants 65 years and above reported significantly greater perceived COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness versus 55-64 years old (t(579) = 2.17, p = .015)). Asian and White participants were more likely to have a good perception of COVID-19 vaccines versus Black and Indigenous (F(6,574) = 2.88, p = .009) participants. Multivariable linear regression revealed that major racial discrimination was the strongest predictor of lower perception of vaccine effectiveness (β = -0.42, p = .006), along with literacy (β = 0.09, p = .002) and identifying as Black compared to White (β = -1.49, p = .020).ConclusionsPerceptions of COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness among 55+ in Canada varied substantially across racial groups, with differences linked to experiences of discrimination and literacy levels. These findings highlight the need for targeted, equity-oriented public health strategies that address both structural racism and misinformation to improve vaccine confidence among older adults in marginalized communities.

articles.title: Impact and cost-effectiveness of national implementation of rotavirus vaccination in Vietnam: A modeling study.
articles.summary: PMID: 42837896. DOI: 10.1016/j.vaccine.2026.129220. BackgroundIn Vietnam, rotavirus remains a leading cause of severe acute gastroenteritis resulting in hospitalization. Although rotavirus vaccines are available in the private sector-primarily accessible to urban children-the Expanded Programme on Immunization has only piloted the vaccine in select provinces. This study assessed the impact and cost-effectiveness of national rotavirus vaccination in Vietnam to inform policy decision on nationwide implementation.MethodsWe used a transparent static cohort model with a granular weekly age structure (< 5 years) to project rotavirus gastroenteritis (RVGE) cases, visits, hospitalizations, and deaths in children under five years, comparing no vaccination to nationwide vaccination with the domestic ROTAVIN vaccine over 10 years starting in 2026. Model inputs drew from global, regional, and local data including pre-vaccine incidence in Vietnam, local vaccine effectiveness and waning data, and treatment costs (governmental and societal perspectives) sourced from a local cost of illness study and hospital records (converted to 2025 USD). Deterministic and probabilistic sensitivity analyses addressed parameter uncertainty.ResultsOver ten years, ROTAVIN vaccination was projected to reduce RVGE health burden by 42%, averting 97,776 (95% uncertainty interval 72,722-342,311) hospital admissions and 433 (330-1300) deaths. The program would cost US$39.5 million ($30.7-$117.7 million) for ten birth cohorts (2026-2036). From the governmental perspective, at least 62% of vaccination costs would be offset by healthcare savings. The cost per DALY averted was estimated at $982 (governmental perspective), while the program was cost-saving from the societal perspective in the base case. Sensitivity analyses confirmed robustness, with a 99% probability of cost-effectiveness from the governmental perspective at a willingness-to-pay threshold of 0.5 times Vietnam's GDP per capita (and 100% from the societal perspective).ConclusionsNationwide ROTAVIN vaccination could avert a substantial health and economic burden in Vietnam and would be highly cost-effective given recently published thresholds.

articles.title: A phase III randomized study: Immunogenicity and safety of a quadrivalent meningococcal conjugate vaccine in healthy adults, adolescents, and children in India and healthy adolescents and children in South Africa.
articles.summary: PMID: 42832931. DOI: 10.1016/j.vaccine.2026.129186. BackgroundMenACYW-TT is a quadrivalent meningococcal conjugate vaccine approved for individuals aged ≥6 weeks. This Phase III study evaluated the immunogenicity and safety of a single dose of MenACYW-TT versus MenACYW-DT and MenPS-ACWY in healthy adults, adolescents, and children in India and in healthy adolescents and children in South Africa.MethodsIn total, 1,328 participants were randomized by age into three cohorts (Cohort Ia: adults aged 18-55 years, India [N=198]; Cohort Ib: adults aged ≥56 years, India [N=200]; Cohort II: children and adolescents aged 2-17 years, India [N=465] and South Africa [N=465]). The immunogenicity of vaccines was assessed with a serum bactericidal assay using human complement (hSBA). The primary objective was to demonstrate the non-inferiority of immunogenicity of a single dose of MenACYW-TT versus MenACYW-DT in children and adolescents aged 2-17 years in terms of hSBA titers in India and South Africa.ResultsThe primary objective was met. The non-inferiority of MenACYW-TT versus MenACYW-DT was demonstrated on post-vaccination Day 30 in participants aged 2-17 years. The lower limit of the 95% confidence interval for the difference in the percentages of the participants achieving seroprotection (hSBA titers ≥1:8) against all four serogroups was greater than -10%. MenACYW-TT demonstrated robust immunogenicity in adults aged 18-55 years and ≥56 years in India. The rates of solicited injection site and systemic reactions were comparable between the participants who received MenACYW-TT versus licensed comparator vaccines. No vaccine-related serious adverse events, study discontinuations, or deaths were reported.ConclusionsA single dose of MenACYW-TT induced non-inferior immune responses and a comparable safety profile versus MenACYW-DT in children and adolescents aged 2-17 years. MenACYW-TT was well tolerated and immunogenic in adults, adolescents, and children in India and in adolescents and children in South Africa.

articles.title: Effect of a comic book-based educational intervention on human papillomavirus vaccine knowledge and safety perception among girls aged 9-14 in Nigeria.
articles.summary: PMID: 42832933. DOI: 10.1016/j.vaccine.2026.129194. BackgroundCervical cancer is a leading cause of death for women and is preventable with the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine and regular screening. However, awareness of vaccines and screenings is poor in many low- and middle-income countries. In 2023, Nigeria sought to deliver 15 million doses of the HPV vaccine to girls aged 9-14. Within this vaccination campaign, we studied the effect of a comic book educational intervention on knowledge and perception of HPV, cervical cancer, and vaccine safety in girls eligible for the vaccine.MethodsThis single-arm study evaluated the effect of a bundled educational intervention on HPV knowledge and safety perception. The three-part intervention was a schoolwide assembly and lecture for children using a culturally tailored comic book as a guide, distribution of the comic book to all the children at the school and then separate focus groups with adult community leaders. The primary outcome was the change in the HPV knowledge score in girls aged 9-14 six weeks post-intervention. Exploratory outcomes were the differential effect of low versus high baseline knowledge, vaccine safety perception, and change in vaccine receipt status at the class level.ResultsWe found significant gains in knowledge across all four states (n = 396; p < 0.01). Classes with lower baseline knowledge gained more from the intervention (p < 0.01). Perception of vaccine safety increased from 62% to 81% (p < 0.01). We did not find a relationship between increased learning and vaccination receipt (p = 0.16).ConclusionAwareness and positive perception of the safety of the HPV vaccine increased following an educational comic book intervention in girls aged 9-14 across Nigeria. Comics may be a low-cost, scalable, and culturally adaptable tool for health education.

articles.title: Circular RNA vaccines encoding Pvs25 induce antibodies that block Plasmodium vivax transmission.
articles.summary: PMID: 42849225. DOI: 10.1016/j.vaccine.2026.129221. Plasmodium vivax is a major malaria parasite that causes acute illness in millions of people each year. Transmission-blocking vaccines (TBVs) could contribute substantially to malaria elimination, although none has yet been approved. We previously demonstrated that a nucleoside-modified mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (mRNA-LNP) vaccine targeting Pvs25, a leading P. vivax TBV antigen, elicited potent and durable transmission-blocking immunity in mice. Emerging evidence suggests that circular RNA (circRNA) may enhance RNA stability, prolong antigen expression, and potentially reduce manufacturing costs compared with conventional linear mRNA. We therefore developed and evaluated two circular Pvs25 RNA-LNP vaccines: one encoding wild-type Pvs25 and another encoding Pvs25 fused to the MHC class I trafficking domain (MITD). Their immunogenicity and functional activity were compared with those of a linear nucleoside-modified Pvs25 mRNA-LNP vaccine. In mice, a single immunization with either the circular RNA or linear mRNA Pvs25 vaccine induced detectable Pvs25-specific antibodies, while booster immunization substantially increased antibody titers and resulted in complete inhibition of P. vivax development in mosquitoes. Both vaccines also elicited robust Pvs25-specific antibody-secreting cell response and cytokine-producing cellular responses. Together, these findings demonstrate the potential of circRNA as a platform for malaria vaccine development and support further evaluation in non-human primates.

articles.title: Reconsidering vaccinate-to-live strategies in EU foot-and-mouth disease control.
articles.summary: PMID: 42837894. DOI: 10.1016/j.vaccine.2026.129217. In January 2025, FMD was detected in water buffalos near Berlin. A few weeks later, a different FMDV-strain was confirmed on dairy farms in Slovakia and Hungary. Since February 2026, Cyprus and Lesvos are confronted with FMD-outbreaks. While Europe is rethinking its FMD-strategies, the two affected member states, Cyprus and Greece, take opposite approaches to control the disease. FMD-vaccination was pivotal for its eradication in many parts of the world. Such regions fought new outbreaks by traditional animal-disease-control. In 2001, a devastating FMD-epizootic swept across the UK and continental Europe. Several million sheep, cattle, and pigs were culled. In the aftermath, OIE (now: WOAH) and EU revised their FMD-strategies. Now, WOAH's Terrestrial Animal Health Code puts strong emphasis on reactive vaccination. An FMD-free status can be regained without slaughtering all vaccinated animals. By contrast, the European FMD Directive of 2003, which contained similar provisions, was repealed. Under the new Delegated Regulation, all restrictions on a vaccination zone are upheld until the last vaccinated animal is removed. Cyprus implemented country-wide FMD-vaccination despite these restrictions. Fearing trade barriers, Greece decided not to vaccinate. Were the consequences not so dramatic, a better head-to-head comparison would hardly be conceivable. Modern FMD-vaccines induce robust immunity after just seven days, minimize virus transmission and allow for DIVA strategies. In addition to the risks posed by global trade and travel, Europe faces major social, economic, and geopolitical challenges. The risk of FMDV incursions is imminent. Cyprus can afford to live with trade restrictions, because export of live animals, raw dairy products and fresh meat only play a minor role in its economy. This would be entirely different if livestock-dense regions in the heart of the continent were affected. The EU must not forgo highly effective and ethically superior control measures that could mitigate socio-economic consequences of future FMD-outbreaks.

articles.title: Mobile-app-based cohort event monitoring study (CEM) of COVID-19 vaccines.
articles.summary: PMID: 42843285. DOI: 10.1016/j.vaccine.2026.129219. Vaccine pharmacovigilance is critically important to ensure transparent information related to vaccine safety. We conducted a prospective, non-interventional, population-based cohort study, SafeVac2.0, in order to supplement passive surveillance of COVID-19 vaccines by collecting self-reported adverse events (AEs). Participation via smartphone app was allowed within 48 h after the administration of the first or second dose of a COVID-19 vaccine. Adverse events were collected up to 3 weeks after the first vaccination, 8 weeks after the second vaccination, and 7 days after the booster dose. Participants were also asked about their health condition 6 and 12 months after the first dose registered. The study was conducted from December 26, 2020 to September 30, 2022. A total of 739,216 persons met the primary inclusion criteria, of which 732,864 documented at least one vaccination. Data on 1,436,039 vaccinations were collected. At least one AE was reported for 68% of the vaccinations and in total 4,007,149 AEs were reported. 88% of AEs consisted of solicited local and systemic reactogenicity. Age, sex, vaccine product and dose were potential predictors for solicited adverse events. The need for medical care was reported in 0.36% of vaccinations. Overall, the study results provide reassurance of the safety profile of COVID-19 vaccines. The use of a native app to monitor self-reported adverse events represents an innovative pharmacovigilance approach.

articles.title: Prospective controlled study of the recombinant zoster vaccine in autoimmune rheumatic disease: robust seroconversion despite intravenous cyclophosphamide.
articles.summary: PMID: 42843284. DOI: 10.1016/j.vaccine.2026.129227. BackgroundRecombinant zoster vaccine (RZV) prevents shingles in autoimmune rheumatic diseases (ARD), but intravenous cyclophosphamide (IVCYC) impact on immunogenicity is unknown. Given cell depletion/cytotoxicity, IVCYC is expected to induce profound immunogenicity impairment, we therefore evaluated its impact.MethodsThis subanalysis of prospective, randomized, placebo-controlled trial included ARD patients receiving IVCYC (ARD-IVCYC) compared with patients without IVCYC (ARD-no IVCYC) and healthy-controls. RZV was administered in two doses. Humoral response (≥4-fold), geometric mean titers (GMT) and cellular response were assessed after second dose. Disease activity and adverse events (AEs) were recorded.ResultsForty-one ARD-IVCYC, 164 ARD-no IVCYC, and 164 controls were included. Seroconversion did not differ between ARD-IVCYC and ARD-no IVCYC (91.9% vs. 91.5%) and were lower than controls (99.4%, p = 0.022). Post-vaccination GMTs were comparable between ARD groups (p > 0.999), but lower than controls (p = 0.006). Cellular response and ARDs flares did not differ between groups (p > 0.05), with no severe AEs.ConclusionRZV elicited >90% humoral response in IVCYC-treated patients, supporting it during IVCYC when warranted (NCT05879419).

articles.title: Longitudinal SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccine immunogenicity in inflammatory bowel disease in relation to anti-TNF therapy and age: a prospective cohort study.
articles.summary: PMID: 42849224. DOI: 10.1016/j.vaccine.2026.129224. BackgroundPatients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) on immunomodulatory therapy may respond less well to vaccination. We followed humoral and cellular responses to SARS-CoV-2 vaccination over 12 months.MethodsIn this single-centre, prospective cohort study, adults with IBD received mRNA vaccine under the Austrian national programme. Two doses were administered 28 days apart and a third dose 6-12 months after the first. S1-RBD IgG, live-virus 50% neutralisation titres (NT50) against wild-type, Delta, Omicron BA.1 and BA.2, and IFN-γ ELISpot responses were measured at baseline and after 3, 6 and 12 months. Associations with anti-TNF therapy and age were analysed with rank-based longitudinal models and with mixed-effects models adjusted for age and sex.ResultsAll 53 twice-vaccinated, infection-naive patients seroconverted at 3 months. Geometric mean (GM) S1-RBD IgG peaked at 3 months (465.7 BAU/ml) and fell by 6 months (124.8 BAU/ml). At 3 months, GM NT50 values were lower against BA.1 (9.0) than against wild-type (24.2) or Delta (26.9), and 13 patients (24.5%) never reached a wild-type NT50 of 1:16. Anti-TNF therapy (32/53, 60.4%) was significantly associated with faster waning. At 6 months, adjusted geometric mean ratio versus other therapy was 0.31 (95% CI 0.20-0.49) for S1-RBD IgG and 0.22 (0.12-0.41) for wild-type NT50. Each additional year of age was associated with 2.4% lower wild-type NT50 (0.976 per year, 95% CI 0.962-0.990). In 33 thrice-vaccinated patients, intercurrent infection (15/33) raised S1-RBD IgG 4.6-fold more than the third dose alone, without a measurable gain in neutralisation. In the adjusted model, IFN-γ ELISpot responses did not differ between treatment groups.DiscussionAnti-TNF therapy and higher age within a relatively young cohort were associated with lower and shorter-lived humoral responses, while cellular responses appeared comparatively preserved. These exploratory associations need confirmation in larger cohorts with clinical endpoints.

articles.title: Sequence-Aware Antigenic Alignment and SRID Potency Interpretation in Influenza Vaccines.
articles.summary: PMID: 42843286. DOI: 10.1016/j.vaccine.2026.129191. Single radial immunodiffusion (SRID) remains the standard potency assay for seasonal influenza vaccines worldwide. Because SRID depends on antigen-antibody recognition, hemagglutinin (HA) sequence variation can influence potency interpretation through its effects on antigenic alignment among vaccine antigens and reference reagents. This review examines the relationship between viral propagation, antigenic fidelity, and reference reagent alignment, and proposes sequence-aware antigenic alignment as a conceptual framework linking HA sequence variation to SRID potency interpretation and harmonization.

articles.title: Assessment of the Fasciola hepatica saposin-like protein 2 (rFhSAP2) vaccine candidate in sheep: Immunogenicity without protective efficacy.
articles.summary: PMID: 42837893. DOI: 10.1016/j.vaccine.2026.129223. Fasciolosis caused by Fasciola hepatica is an economically important parasitic disease of livestock and a major zoonotic disease in humans. Vaccination is a promising strategy to reduce the impact of fasciolosis and dependence on fasciolicides. Saposin-like protein 2 (FhSAP2) has previously shown high immunogenicity and reductions in fluke burden in experimental animal models; however, its efficacy has not been evaluated in sheep. Twenty-one female sheep were randomly assigned to three groups (n = 7): vaccinated, adjuvant control, and infection control. The vaccinated group received 400 μg of rtFhSAP2 formulated with Montanide ISA 201 VG, the adjuvant control received Montanide ISA 201 VG alone, and the infection control received saline. Animals received three subcutaneous immunizations at four-week intervals and were subsequently challenged orally with 200 F. hepatica metacercariae. Vaccine efficacy was evaluated based on fluke burden, fecal egg counts, and egg viability. Antigen-specific IgG, IgG1, and IgG2 antibody responses were assessed by ELISA. Vaccination with rtFhSAP2 resulted in a 16.4% reduction in fluke burden compared with the infection control group (p > 0.05). Reductions in fecal egg counts ranged from 8.9% to 34.5% (p > 0.05). Fecal egg viability remained high, ranging from 88.9% to 91.3% among groups (p > 0.05). Gallbladder-derived egg viability was lower in vaccinated sheep (56.9%) than in the infection control (75.9%) and adjuvant control (73.6%) groups (p > 0.05). Vaccination induced a strong and sustained humoral response. IgG and IgG1 levels were significantly higher in vaccinated sheep than in both control groups from weeks 4-24 and 4-32, respectively. IgG2 levels were also significantly higher from weeks 4-24, although the response was lower than that of IgG1. Overall, rtFhSAP2 formulated with Montanide ISA 201 VG was highly immunogenic in sheep, but the humoral response did not translate into significant protection against F. hepatica.

articles.title: Environmental Chemicals as Modifiers of the Association between Age and Ovarian Reserve
articles.summary: ObjectiveTo evaluate whether the well-established age-related reduction in antral follicle counts (AFC) is greater among women with higher concentrations of endocrine-disrupting chemicals. DesignProspective cohort study using the doubly robust (DR) learner, a flexible machine learning method that models the relationship between an exposure and outcome of interest and identifies potential modifiers of this relation. SubjectsSeven hundred seventy-five women aged 18-45 years enrolled in The Environment and Reproductive Health (EARTH) Study at the Massachusetts General Hospital Fertility Center, Boston, USA, between 2004 and 2019. ExposureAge at AFC assessment calculated as the date of antral follicle scan minus the patients birthdate, categorized into <35 years or [≥]35 years. We assessed urinary concentrations of 16 endocrine-disrupting chemicals, including 11 urinary phthalate metabolites, 3 urinary parabens, urinary bisphenol A, and hair mercury, as potential modifiers of the age-AFC association. Main Outcome MeasuresAFC assessed by transvaginal ultrasonography. ResultsIn this cohort of 775 women, 43% were less than 35 years of age. Women greater than or equal to aged 35 years had lower AFC (mean [SD]: 11.63 [6.24] vs. 16.89 [8.64]) Four endocrine-disrupting chemicals significantly modified the age-AFC association. Women with higher urinary mono-isobutyl phthalate (MiBP), monocarboxyisooctyl phthalate (MCOP), and mono(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (MEHP) concentrations experienced stronger negative associations between age and AFC. Analyses revealed that the age-AFC association strengthened, declining at a faster rate when MiBP, MCOP, or MEHP concentrations were higher. Women with higher hair Hg concentrations experienced weaker negative associations between age and AFC. The remaining 12 endocrine-disrupting chemicals did not modify the age-AFC relationship. ConclusionSelect phthalate metabolites, specifically MiBP, MCOP, and MEHP, were associated with a modified age-related decline in ovarian reserve in a dose-dependent manner. These findings, though limited, add to the growing evidence that certain phthalates are associated with a steeper age-related decline in AFC. What this study addsUsing the DR-Learner, a flexible machine learning approach designed to identify effect modifiers among a large set of candidates, we evaluated whether 16 endocrine-disrupting chemicals modify the well-established association between age and ovarian reserve. Three phthalate metabolites (MiBP, MCOP, MEHP) strengthened the negative age-antral follicle count association; for MiBP and MCOP this pattern was curvilinear and dose-dependent, with apparent concentration thresholds above which the age-related decline accelerated. Hair mercury was associated with a weaker negative association, possibly reflecting protective effects of seafood-derived omega-3 fatty acids. We discuss important limitations, but note that our findings add to evidence that higher phthalate concentrations accompany a stronger negative age-AFC association.

articles.title: Designed nanofiber immunogens prime antibody responsesto diverse conformations of the HIV-1 fusion peptide
articles.summary: Focusing antibody responses towards known neutralizing epitopes is a major strategy for protective immunization. Targeting flexible antigenic regions represents a unique challenge because functional antibodies must be able to bind the epitope of interest in multiple conformations. The fusion peptide (FP) of HIV-1 is a flexible peptide critical to viral entry of host cells for which broadly neutralizing antibodies have been identified. Because elicitation of potent, functional antibodies toward this epitope remains an unmet challenge in HIV-1 vaccination, we introduce a designed immunogen platform capable of raising anti-FP-antibodies with increased conformational tolerance relative to a traditional carrier protein. Antibodies induced by these immunogens bind heterologous FP sequences when elicited in mice and infant non-human primates. This platform shows promise for preclinical development to prime antibody responses toward FP of the HIV-1 envelope and can likely be translated to peptide immunofocusing for other viral pathogens.
